inclusion_rule: Setting (one definition for all four topics): text entry by spelling, in any signal type in the wiki (neural, EMG, EOG, EPG, video, ultrasound and others): studies whose full text, reference list removed, names a speller, letter-by-letter entry, or spelling out words, letters or sentences. Boundary: acoustic-only systems are outside the wiki; mentions in related work, reviews and unrelated uses of 'spelling' enter, so every count is an upper bound (pattern match); versions are counted once; the target's three versions are excluded; the usual approach is counted at the target's time (index year 2022 or earlier, target first public 2022-11). Design compared: the user action that selects each letter: evoked-potential speller (P300, SSVEP, RSVP), motor or cursor selection (point-and-click, virtual keyboard, motor imagery), attempted handwriting, NATO or radio-alphabet code words, other speech production of letters. A study counts under every action its text names.

usual_approach.note: Curated prior set (22): evoked-potential speller 8, spoken letter names decoded from lip video 7, motor or cursor selection 4, handwriting or imagined characters 2, eye movement 1, code words 0. matched set to null in slots.json at the coordinator's request.

read_fulltext.quote: Overall, four different grammar models were tested: sentence construction grammar, unrestricted NATO grammar, NL equivalence grammar, and unigram grammar.

A total of 4 subjects were presented with 1200 word-sequences (mean words/phrase = 6.0) generated from a relatively small 202-word vocabulary, including words and numbers associated with a special operations silent-speech data set (US Army 2009), the NATO alphabet and commonly used English phrases
Participant T5 averaged 36.1 ± 0.9 and 39.2 ± 1.2 ccpm for the QWERTY and OPTI-II keyboards, respectively.
typing rates were high, plateauing at 90 characters per minute with a 5.4% character error rate
Typing speed is user-regulated, reaching 110 characters per minute, resulting in 22 words per minute with a word error rate of 1.6%.
Across 19 sessions after freezing the classifier, we observed a mean classification accuracy of 96.8% (99% CI [94.5, 98.6])
On a continuous spelling task, visual-alone recognition of 45-55%
SilentSpeller focuses on recognizing the 26 letters of the alphabet, silently mouthed in the context of spelling a word.
with T17 reaching a peak of 47 characters per minute and T18 reaching 110 characters per minute

state_of_the_art.metric: peak online character rate, attempted finger typing (QWERTY), intracortical, participant T18 (T17 peak 47), 5-gram language model, 1.6% WER
state_of_the_art.note: Outside the spelling text pattern; confirmed state of the art of the published table M04/neural-text-entry-action. Best value among this topic's ledger candidates: 90 characters per minute, attempted handwriting, 2021 (doi-10.1038-s41586-021-03506-2), read.

prior_period_counts_superseded.definition: unique studies in the topic population dated 2022 or earlier by index year (target first public 2022-11; the 2022 studies fall in the prior or [concurrent] window), target versions excluded; full-text pattern match with the reference list removed, upper bounds (mentions and reviews count)

prior_period_counts.cutoff: Target reference date 2021-12-22 (received; published 2022-11-08; no preprint in the wiki). Prior: first public before 2021-06-22. [Concurrent]: 2021-06-22 to 2022-06-22: Chaudhary 2022-03 (implanted auditory-neurofeedback speller), SilentSpeller 2022-04-29 (silent letter names, electropalatography); Moses 2021-07 is a direct-word decoder, not a speller. Dated 2021 with month unresolved, not counted: pmc-8226883-p300autoencoder, pmc-7916479-ssvepdataset. Undated index rows were dated from manifests (1994-2003 lip-reading spelling studies prior; SilentSpeller concurrent; the rest later or off-population).
prior_period_counts.cleaning: Population cleaned from the 482-study full-text pattern set: reviews removed (71 by title in all years), and studies that only mention spellers removed; kept are the 22 prior studies that build, test or record a spelling or text-entry system or spelled-letter recognition (classified from ledger records and titles). Excluded as off-population: finger-spelling and sign studies, Brain2Char (speech-to-character decoding), corpora with only a few spelled words.
prior_period_counts.tier: pattern match, curated by study design (not mentions)
